summary: A 1931 lookout on a water tank and a 1938 K-brace tower that straddles it, on University of California land near Lick Observatory; not legally open to the public.

facts.design: Special K-brace tower (Plan L-901), 13 ft high, with a standard live-in cab (Plan BC-301), built to straddle a 10,000-gallon concrete water tank

access.note: Not legally open to the public. SummitPost advises asking the patrol officer at Lick Observatory for permission.

visit.trail_note: Hiking is the only way to the summit; permission is needed to go up

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1931/1938: 1931 for the first lookout, set on a water tank, and 1938 for the present K-brace tower and cab that straddle that tank. The record's Wikidata value (1938) matches the later structure, and the 1931 date matches the first lookout.

notes_for_editor: The build history rests on the register alone: 1931 for the first lookout on a water tank, 1938 for the present K-brace tower. No second source explains the sequence. The record's Wikidata value (1938) is noted only. Access and the hiking-only route come from SummitPost, a climbing guide, so treat them as secondary; the register does not describe public access. No NRHP listing, staffing record or visit report was found, so the staffing status is unknown. The FFLA list gives only 'Standing'. The 2020 SCU Lightning Complex coverage found in search concerns Lick Observatory and is not about this lookout, so it is left out. Access level 'permission' is my reading of the SummitPost advice; the register does not state a permit rule. Read budget: three page reads; the cached FFLA and Wikipedia-list pages were checked locally.
